content: Export pipeline (docs.expo.dev SDK 57): Print.printToFileAsync({html}) renders PDF and writes to the app CACHE directory (FilePrintResult.uri, base64 optional); margins on Android via @page CSS; iOS can't load local asset URLs in HTML (base64-inline). Therefore writing to Downloads REQUIRES a second step. expo-file-system legacy module (expo-file-system/legacy) provides StorageAccessFramework (Android, works in Expo Go): requestDirectoryPermissionsAsync() -> {granted, directoryUri} (Android 11+; user picks Downloads once, persist directoryUri), createFileAsync(parentUri, fileName, mimeType) — fileName WITHOUT extension, returns SAF content:// URI; writeAsStringAsync(safUri, contents, {encoding:'base64'}) for binary; SAF URIs cannot be moved (moveAsync destination must be file://). iOS: no Downloads equivalent — expo-sharing shareAsync(uri, {UTI:'.pdf', mimeType:'application/pdf'}) is the pattern. SheetJS: npm 'xlsx' latest is still 0.18.5 (stale since 2022, CVE-2023-30533 in npm-distributed versions); install from cdn.sheetjs.com per official docs; XLSX.write(wb,{type:'base64'}) then writeAsStringAsync with base64 encoding.
